text: When I was eight, I knew vampires were real.
Every night, Gran poured rice along my windowsill.
They can't help themselves, she'd whisper. They must count every grain.
And by then... the sun is up.
I'm thirty-four now. Gran's gone. I moved into her house.
She'd covered every mirror in it.
Vampires aren't real. So tonight, I swept the rice away.
Three a.m. Something woke me.
A voice. Counting.
Four hundred and six. Four hundred and seven.
It wasn't coming from outside.
It was closer.
I was on the floor, sorting rice into neat little piles.
And the voice... was mine.
I pulled the cloth off Gran's mirror.
The room was there. The rice was there.
I wasn't.
The rice was never meant to keep them out.
Gran was keeping me in.
I've finished counting.
It's still dark.
And the window... is open.
One.
